title: Development and construction of MAROON-X
what_was_studied: Red-optical architecture, pupil slicer, double scrambler and rubidium-referenced etalon concept
numerical_result: The planned intrinsic per-measurement noise floor was below 1 m/s; the paper described construction rather than on-sky performance
remaining_question: The original Magellan deployment plan changed before commissioning at Gemini North

title: MAROON-X a radial velocity spectrograph for the Gemini Observatory
what_was_studied: Dual-arm completion, science detectors, telescope front end and laboratory stability tests
numerical_result: Laboratory tests indicated sub-m/s simultaneous-reference calibration capability
remaining_question: Laboratory calibration did not yet measure telescope illumination or stellar variability

title: On-sky commissioning of MAROON-X
what_was_studied: Installation and commissioning of the dual-arm instrument at Gemini North
numerical_result: Delivered in June 2019 and commissioned as a visiting instrument; the reported resolving power is about 85000 over 500 to 920 nm
remaining_question: Commissioning results require run and detector-era labels for long-baseline use

title: MAROON-X the first two years of EPRVs from Gemini North
what_was_studied: First two years of operations and radial-velocity observations
numerical_result: Regular sub-m/s on-sky performance and a short-term instrumental floor near 0.30 m/s were reported
remaining_question: Short-term precision did not remove run-to-run offsets or long-term etalon drift

title: MAROON-X 24A data reduction issues
what_was_studied: Effects of an earthquake and observatory power loss on the echelle image and reduction
numerical_result: Gemini stated that existing 2024A radial velocities were uncertain at about 20 m/s while 2024B data appeared within specification
remaining_question: Reprocessed 2024A products and a quantitative recovery assessment were not linked from the notice

title: Calibrating the instrumental drift in MAROON-X using an ensemble analysis
what_was_studied: Eleven-star ensemble used to infer observing-run offsets from September 2020 to January 2024
numerical_result: Etalon drift was about 0.022 m/s/day; run offsets were calibrated to about 0.5 m/s and HD 3651 residual RMS was below 0.70 m/s over 29 months
remaining_question: The ensemble model depends on assumptions about reference-star signals and needs validation across later incidents and eras
